chunks: And from him (Al-Haytham ibn Adi) from Hammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said:
Three things do not break the fast of the fasting person: vomiting, seminal emission, and cupping. And he (peace be upon him) did not see any harm in using kohl (eye medicine) for the fasting person.
And indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) underwent cupping while he was fasting.
ai.seo_question: What acts do not break the fast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential principle that external medical interventions, such as cupping and the application of kohl, do not break the fast because they do not involve the consumption of substantial nourishment reaching the stomach. By citing the Prophet’s practice, it reinforces the Shia view that these acts are permissible, distinguishing them from acts that explicitly nullify the fast, while highlighting the scholarly consensus on the non-invalidating nature of involuntary bodily functions like vomiting and emission.
